Similar business development will dominate the south side of Lincoln Highway in the Village of Matteson from the Illinois Central Railroad tracks west to Cicero Avenue, except for the cemetery land and the residential area immediately to the east of it.
The general area of Chicago Heights is best described as that of a subcenter, interacting with the greater metropolitan area. This general area has developed along major transportation routes, both railways and highways emanating from the City of Chicago.
Interstate Route 80 has been constructed to the north of Lincoln Highway and there is a proposed east-west freeway under study in a corridor several miles to the south. The eastern terminus of the proposed improvement is controlled by a newly completed improvement from Chicago Road eastward through the City of Chicago Heights. To the west, the location of the improvement is fixed by the recently constructed interchange between Lincoln Highway and Interstate Highway 57 and the recently improved intersection at Lincoln Highway and Cicero Avenue.
These considerations in conjunction with the extensive residential and commercial development, long established in the area through which this improvement will pass have limited the location of this improvement to the present highway location. The combined design study considered how to best accommodate the highway improvement largely within the existing right-of-way with as little land taking and disruption to business and neighborhood values as possible while improving the alignment, safety and traffic carrying capabilities.
J. Inventory of Economic Factors
The information about the four effected communities discussed below, was obtained from the <u>Suburban Factook</u>, 1973 compiled by the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission.
1. Chicago Heights
The City of Chicago Heights
The City of Chicago Heights has 15,812 residents over 16 years of age who are employed. 19.4% of this number are employed in professional or managerial positions, 26.4% are employed in clerical or sales positions, 36% work as craftsmen or opperatives, 4.8% are laborers or farmers, and 13.4% are employed in service type position. 81.2% of the Chicago Heights' working population commute by automobile.
